Subject: Post-call: TCO anchoring, budget cap & pilot ops

Hi Anita / Jonah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned and can move to a minimal pilot that stays inside your procurement guardrails. I’ve bolded the asks / commitments at the end.

High-level takeaway
- Primary goal: reduce fraud-review manual work and accelerate dispute routing by surfacing higher-confidence predictions at ingest. That translates to less manual triage and faster merchant payouts.
- Top constraint: procurement has a hard cap of ~$30k/month for an initial pilot/PO window. Finance wants line-item clarity before sign-off.

Observed volumes (your numbers + our assumptions)- Generated text calls (customer message rewrites + classification): ~150M tokens/month
- Embeddings for similarity/lookup: ~600k vectors/month
- Peak concurrency requirement: sub-300ms token-latency for high-priority paths

Cost levers we discussed and how they map to LumenPay
- Continuous batching: batching across short windows can reduce per-token GPU time by ~2.5–4x depending on request mix. For your traffic mix we estimate ~3x on average.
- Prefix/KV caching: common system prompts + user prefixes show up in ~40% of requests — caching those reduces repeated decode tokens by ~25–35%.
- Model selection & quantization: switching to a quantized variant (int8) for higher-volume paths yields ~20–35% savings with a modest quality delta.
- Dedicated vs hosted routing: a reserved dedicated pool (monthly commit) reduces per-token infra cost and provides predictable throughput; blended price for the pilot model is materially lower than pure on-demand hosted.

Proposed minimal pilot (4 weeks) — design to stay under the $30k cap
- Scope: 2 production routes (classification + response draft) + embeddings for similarity on a 2% live sample (shadowed for accuracy testing).
- Expected effective token volume for pilot: ~12–20M gen tokens + 120k embeddings (we’ll refine once we get your sampled logs).
- Pricing approach: line-item estimate (model hours + per-token charges + inferred infra uplift + operational support). I will send an XLSX line-item that includes both hosted and dedicated equivalent pricing and a blended ROI page.
- Acceptance criteria: accuracy within agreed thresholds (precision lift > 12% vs baseline on the sampled set), latency SLO for priority traffic < 350ms p95, and no data leakage in transit/storage.

Immediate next steps
1) I’ll email the line-item pricing workbook + ROI workbook by Monday — action (Marcus).
2) Anita / Jonah to confirm procurement contact (PO & legal) and whether SOC2 evidence is required inside the PO timeframe — action (LumenPay).
3) If the line-item fits the $30k cap, we’ll provision pilot infra and target a start date two weeks after PO.

Attachments I’ll include: redwood-pilot-pricing.xlsx (line-items), roi-workbook.xlsx (simple sensitivity analysis).

If that matches what you heard, I’ll finalize the XLSX with separate tabs for: baseline hosted estimate, dedicated-reserved estimate (monthly commit), caching/batching sensitivity, and a 4-week pilot runbook.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — this matches our read. A couple of clarifying points from procurement/finance before we can route a PO: 

1) The $30k/month cap is non-negotiable for the pilot PO window. If the line-item estimate pushes us above that we will need an internal exec approval and longer lead time.
2) We need one consolidated spreadsheet that shows: hosted vs reserved committed cost (monthly), line items for tokens vs infra vs support, and a worst-case sensitivity (20% overage) with the cost owner called out.
3) SOC2 evidence is required for any pilot that touches production data. We can accept an attestation + SOC2 report snapshot in the procurement packet if Redwood can provide it within the PO period.

Procurement contact: procurement@lumenpay.com (cc’d). Jonah (CFO) will review the spreadsheet and confirm by EOD Tuesday if we can proceed to PO. If Jonah signs off, procurement will issue a PO and we’ll aim for a pilot start ~2 weeks after PO is in place.

One more ask — can you include a short contingency plan (bullet list) for cost overruns and a rollback/fallback path if model quality is out of tolerance? Procurement wants explicit gates.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Anita Sharma
Head of Product Operations | LumenPay
